cards.name: 3D Channel Extract
cards.summary: Turns an auxiliary 3D channel stored in a multichannel render (RPF/EXR from a 3D app: Z-depth, object ID, normals, UVs) into a visible greyscale or colour image. On ordinary footage it shows nothing useful.
use_for: Turn a 3D render's Z-depth into a greyscale map to use as the Blur Map of Camera Lens Blur (precompose it first)
Preview which aux channels a CGI render actually carries before compositing
Build a depth matte for colour-grading the background of a 3D title shot separately
avoid: Applying it to camera footage, stock video or press photos: there is no 3D channel, so the output is blank or flat
Leaving Black/White Point at defaults: the depth range of the render rarely matches, giving a solid black or white frame

params.name: Black Point
params.does: Channel value mapped to black (depth units from the 3D app)
params.typical: nearest scene depth of the render

params.name: White Point
params.typical: farthest scene depth of the render

cards.scripting: Only works on a layer whose source is an RPF or multichannel EXR with aux channels; there is no Premiere equivalent. Black Point / White Point are in the 3D app's depth units, so read the render's range first (Info panel shows 3D channel values while the effect is selected). For multichannel EXRs whose passes AE does not map to its 3D channels, use EXtractoR instead. 3D Channel popup order (Z-Depth, Object ID, Texture UV, Surface Normals, Coverage, Background RGB, Unclamped RGB, Material ID) is from Adobe docs, not from the harvest: verify before relying on indices above 1.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an RPF/EXR with 3D aux channels; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Cryptomatte
cards.summary: Picks per-object or per-material mattes out of a Cryptomatte EXR render by clicking objects, giving clean anti-aliased isolation of any CG element. Without Cryptomatte layers in the EXR it produces nothing.
use_for: Isolate one building, prop or vehicle in a 3D render to grade or glow it separately
Cut out a CG logo or map element for a trailer or explainer composite
Mask a 3D object to place text behind it
avoid: Any footage that is not a Cryptomatte EXR from Blender, C4D, Houdini, Maya etc.
Expecting a script to pick objects: the selection lives in the custom Settings data

params.name: Output
params.does: What the effect outputs (popup, 4 options, 1-based): 1 Colors (colour-coded IDs), 2 Matted Colors, 3 Matted RGBA, 4 Matte Only (read from After Effects 26.0)
params.typical: the matte option once objects are picked (check the label in the UI)

params.name: Selection Mode
params.does: Toggles interactive click-to-pick mode in the Composition panel

cards.scripting: Needs a multichannel EXR containing Cryptomatte layers. The layer choice and the picked object keys are stored in the custom 'Settings' property, which cannot be set from a spec; save a configured instance as a .ffx animation preset and apply that preset instead. Output: 1 Colors, 2 Matted Colors, 3 Matted RGBA, 4 Matte Only (read from After Effects 26.0).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a Cryptomatte EXR and custom Settings data; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Depth Matte
cards.summary: Reads the Z-depth channel of a 3D render (RPF/EXR) and keeps only the parts nearer or farther than a chosen depth, creating a depth-based transparency matte. Does nothing on normal footage.
use_for: Separate foreground and background of a CG render so a title can sit between them
Cut a 3D city or map render at a depth to reveal a layer behind
Make depth-based layers for a parallax trailer shot
avoid: Live-action or stock footage: no depth channel, so the layer goes fully opaque or fully transparent
Zero Feather on aliased depth renders: jagged edges

params.name: Depth
params.does: Depth value where the cut happens (3D app units)
params.typical: a value between the render's near and far depth

params.name: Feather
params.typical: small, a few percent of the scene depth range

cards.scripting: Source layer must be an RPF or EXR with a Z-depth aux channel. Depth/Feather are in the 3D application's units; use 3D Channel Extract first to read the range. No Premiere equivalent.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a Z-depth channel from an RPF/EXR; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Depth of Field
cards.summary: Simulates camera focus on a 3D render by blurring pixels according to their distance from a focal plane read from the Z-depth channel. On footage without a depth channel nothing happens.
use_for: Add focus falloff to a CG render of a building, map or product
Rack focus between foreground and background objects in a 3D trailer shot
Soften a busy 3D background behind a title
avoid: Camera footage or photos: use Camera Lens Blur with a depth map or a mask instead
Large Maximum Radius on edges with no coverage data: halos around objects

params.name: Focal Plane
params.does: Depth that stays sharp (3D app units)

params.name: Maximum Radius
params.does: Largest blur radius for out-of-focus areas

params.name: Focal Plane Thickness
params.does: Depth range around the focal plane that stays sharp

params.name: Focal Bias
params.does: How fast blur ramps up away from the focal plane

cards.scripting: Needs an RPF/EXR layer with a Z-depth channel; this is not AE's camera depth of field (that is a camera layer setting) and not Camera Lens Blur. Focal Plane is in the 3D app's depth units: for a rack focus keyframe Focal Plane from the near object's depth to the far object's depth (read both with 3D Channel Extract / the Info panel; no generic values work across renders).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a Z-depth channel from an RPF/EXR; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: EXtractoR
cards.summary: fnord ProEXR plug-in bundled with AE that pulls any channel set (render passes such as diffuse, specular, AO, depth) out of a multichannel EXR and maps it into RGB/alpha for compositing.
use_for: Rebuild a CG shot from its EXR passes so lighting can be tweaked in the comp
Pull a depth or AO pass from an EXR to drive blur or shading
Extract a mask pass from a 3D render for an explainer graphic
avoid: Single-layer EXRs or normal footage: nothing extra to extract
Scripted use without a preset: the channel mapping is custom data

params.name: Black Point
params.typical: 0 for colour passes, near depth for Z

params.name: White Point
params.typical: 1 for colour passes, far depth for Z

params.name: UnMult
params.does: Un-premultiplies the extracted channels by alpha

cards.scripting: Which EXR layer/channels go to R, G, B, A is stored in the custom 'Channel Info' property, which cannot be set from a spec; configure it once in the UI and save an .ffx animation preset, then apply the preset. Black/White Point are 32-bit float values; work in a 32-bpc project for unclamped passes.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a multichannel EXR and custom Channel Info data; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Fog 3D
cards.summary: Adds atmospheric fog that thickens with distance, using the Z-depth channel of a 3D render (RPF/EXR) to decide how much fog each pixel gets.
use_for: Add depth haze to a CG city or landscape render for a documentary opener
Push background buildings back in a 3D map flythrough
Moody trailer atmosphere on a 3D environment
avoid: Camera footage: no depth channel, so it either fogs the whole frame flat or does nothing; use a gradient + Fractal Noise instead
Pure white fog at 100% opacity: washes out the whole render

params.name: Fog Color
params.typical: #C8D2DC cool grey or a warm haze tone

params.name: Fog Start Depth
params.does: Depth where fog begins (3D app units)

params.name: Fog End Depth
params.does: Depth where fog is at full density

params.name: Scattering Density
params.does: How quickly fog builds up between start and end

params.name: Layer Contribution
params.does: How much the optional gradient layer modulates the fog
params.typical: 0 unless a Gradient Layer is set

cards.scripting: Needs an RPF/EXR layer with Z-depth. 'Gradient Layer' is a layer-reference property: set it to a layer index in the comp from script, not through the spec. Fog Color is a colour property: pass "#RRGGBB".

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a Z-depth channel from an RPF/EXR; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: ID Matte
cards.summary: Creates a matte that isolates one object or material from a 3D render, using the Object ID or Material ID aux channel stored in an RPF/EXR file.
use_for: Isolate one object in an older RPF-based 3D render to grade it
Mask a specific material (glass, screen) in a CG product shot
avoid: Ordinary footage: no ID channel, so the whole layer disappears or stays
Modern Cryptomatte EXRs: use the Cryptomatte effect instead, it gives cleaner edges

params.name: Aux. Channel
params.does: Which ID channel to read: Object ID or Material ID (popup, 1-based)
params.typical: match the channel the render carries

params.name: ID Selection
params.does: ID number of the object/material to keep
params.typical: the ID read with the Info panel

params.name: Invert
params.does: Keep everything except the selected ID

params.name: Use Coverage
params.does: Uses the coverage channel for anti-aliased edges

cards.scripting: Needs an RPF/EXR layer with Object ID or Material ID channels. Aux. Channel: 1 Material ID, 2 Object ID (the default) (read from After Effects 26.0).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an Object/Material ID channel from an RPF/EXR; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: IDentifier
cards.summary: fnord ProEXR plug-in that reads an object/material ID channel in a multichannel EXR and shows it as random colours or outputs a matte for a chosen ID number.
use_for: Visualise object IDs in a 3D render to find the right ID number
Matte out one object from an EXR render for a separate grade or glow
avoid: Footage without an integer ID channel: shows nothing
Hard ID edges on moving objects: use Cryptomatte when the render provides it

params.name: Display
params.does: Output mode: colour-coded IDs or a matte (popup, 1-based)
params.typical: 1 to inspect, a matte mode to cut

params.name: ID
params.typical: ID read from the colour view

cards.scripting: The EXR channel to read is chosen in the custom 'Channel Info' property, which cannot be set from a spec; use a saved .ffx preset. Display: 1 Colors, 2 Luma Matte, 3 Alpha Matte, 4 Raw (read from After Effects 26.0).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs an EXR ID channel and custom Channel Info data; the photo reference has none), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Backwards
cards.summary: Plays the layer's audio in reverse; optional left/right channel swap. Video is unaffected.
use_for: Reverse a cymbal or whoosh to build a riser into a trailer hit
Rewind sound for a 'let's go back' moment in an explainer
Reverse-reverb swell into a news sting: put Reverb above Backwards in the effect stack
avoid: Reversing dialogue under on-screen speech: sounds broken
Expecting the picture to reverse too: use Time Remap or Time-Reverse Layer for video

params.name: Swap Channels
params.does: Swaps left and right channels while reversing

cards.scripting: Audio effect: needs a layer with audio, nothing visible (status needs_input). Reversal happens simply by applying the effect; Swap Channels is a 0/1 checkbox. Only audible on layers with audio. Premiere has no reverse-audio effect: reverse a clip there via Speed/Duration 'Reverse Speed'.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (audio-only effect, nothing visible to render), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Bass & Treble
cards.summary: Simple two-knob tone control that boosts or cuts low (bass) and high (treble) frequencies of the layer's audio.
use_for: Add low-end weight to a trailer hit or music bed
Brighten a muffled VO or interview clip
Thin out music under narration by cutting bass
avoid: Big bass boosts on voice: boomy and can clip
Precise EQ work: use Parametric EQ instead
cards.scripting: Audio effect: needs a layer with audio, nothing visible (status needs_input). Values are relative -100..100 (not dB). Premiere splits this into separate 'Bass' and 'Treble' effects.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (audio-only effect, nothing visible to render), so no gallery frame was rendered.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: not_rendered is right (audio-only, test footage has no audio stream), but demo Bass 50 / Treble 30 and recipe Bass 40 sat outside the card's own typical range and in its 'can clip' avoid; set demo Bass 25 / Treble 20 and recipe Bass 0->25

cards.name: Compressor
cards.summary: Dynamic range compressor that turns down audio louder than a threshold, evening out loud and soft parts of voice or music, with makeup gain and an output limit.
use_for: Even out a VO or interview so quiet words stay audible under music
Glue and punch up a trailer music bed
Tame peaks in a phone-recorded news clip
avoid: Very high ratio with fast release on voice: pumping and breathing artefacts
Too much makeup gain: raises background noise and hiss

params.name: Ratio (x:1)
params.does: How strongly signal above threshold is reduced

params.name: Knee (db)
params.does: Softness of the transition around threshold

cards.scripting: Audio effect: needs a layer with audio, nothing visible (status needs_input). Premiere's closest match is Single-band Compressor (Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release, Gain). Property names include units in brackets and the knee uses lowercase 'db': 'Knee (db)'. Auto Release is a 0/1 checkbox; with it on, Release (ms) is probably largely ignored (not verified). Final loudness normalisation is better done in Premiere or at export.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (audio-only effect, nothing visible to render), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Delay
cards.summary: Echo effect that repeats the audio after a set time, with feedback for multiple repeats and separate dry/wet levels.
use_for: Echo tail on the last word of a trailer line or title hit
Slapback on a whoosh or impact for extra size
Stylised echo on a quote for a dramatic documentary moment
avoid: Feedback above about 70: repeats pile up and get muddy (the harvested 0-1000 range is not a usable range)
Echo on full narration: hurts intelligibility

params.name: Feedback
params.does: How much echo is fed back for repeats

cards.scripting: Audio effect: needs a layer with audio, nothing visible (status needs_input). Harvested ranges go above 100 for Delay Amount/Feedback (0-1000) and Dry/Wet Out (0-400); stay within 0-100 for sane results. Echo throw: keep Wet Out at 0 and jump it to 75 at the start of the last word (the recipe's 1.95/2.0 s stand for that word's time; replace them) and extend the layer so the tail can ring out. Premiere's Delay has only Delay, Feedback, Mix.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (audio-only effect, nothing visible to render), so no gallery frame was rendered.
